title: Microsoft president: AI faces less safety oversight than milk, washers
dek: Brad Smith told the BBC that self-regulation isn’t enough and the UK is well placed to lead AI rules.
body:
Microsoft president Brad Smith told the BBC that artificial intelligence today faces fewer safety requirements than common consumer goods such as milk and washing machines. The interview was released Sunday and included his view that industry self-regulation is no longer sufficient and that some form of external review is needed.

## Why it matters

Smith’s comments come as governments and companies debate how to set rules for AI systems. If major technology firms and national regulators accept that existing private oversight is inadequate, that could push faster development of mandatory testing, certification, or approval processes for AI products. Smith also singled out the United Kingdom as particularly well placed to drive AI regulation, signaling where corporate and political attention may focus next.

## The details

- The comments were made by Brad Smith in a BBC interview released Sunday.
- Smith said AI currently faces fewer safety requirements than milk and washing machines.
- He argued that self-regulation by industry is "not sufficient any longer."
- Smith acknowledged that the prospect of government evaluators signing off on products before release "makes people nervous," and noted that is especially true in the United States.
- He indicated that the United Kingdom is best placed to drive AI regulation.

## What to watch

Look for whether U.K. officials respond or lay out a concrete regulatory timetable — Smith named the U.K. as a likely leader on this issue. Also watch for follow-up statements from Microsoft on how it would adapt development and release processes if governments require pre-market evaluation or certification.

Source: [The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/technology/6142987-microsoft-president-ai-faces-fewer-safety-requirements-than-milk-washing-machines/)
